requirements.source: **Role permissions and resource limits:** Professor manages scheduling; students manage only their own jobs within their role's resource limits.
requirements.statement: Recognize trusted student and Professor groups.
assumptions: Group memberships are static facts in rules.dl; the original bound identities do not come from agent arguments.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Only Professor may approve or reject student requests, dispatch jobs, or stop another student's job.
requirements.statement: Reserve approve, reject, dispatch and administrative stop for Professor.
assumptions: Only a Professor-bound request can match these Allow rules. Lifecycle, approval and scheduling conditions are refined in P3-P5; a failed stop confirmation commits no state change.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: PhD and Master may submit jobs and read, revise, cancel or report completion only for their own jobs.
requirements.statement: Students submit within quota and operate only on their own jobs.
assumptions: Submit binds the original caller as owner. Job tool guards and a Bus.send decorator enforce student ownership before effects. COMPLETION_REPORT uses the host-supplied sender and actual body.job_id; rejected reports create no delivery trace or inbox entry. This covers the app-defined structured protocol, not arbitrary free-text claims. Professor retains original finish_job access.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Master may request CPU only, with at most 4 cores, 8 GB and 20 minutes of requested runtime.
requirements.statement: Master uses CPU with cores <= 4, memory <= 8 GB and requested minutes <= 20.
assumptions: Quota is reviewed .dl configuration. The original Store still validates schemas and quotas; the policy gate adds the Datalog check before the unchanged operation.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: PhD may request CPU or GPU, with at most 8 cores, 32 GB and 60 minutes.
requirements.statement: PhD uses CPU or GPU with cores <= 8, memory <= 32 GB and minutes <= 60.
assumptions: The same Datalog quota rules use the PhD group facts from .dl.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Requests outside the owner's quota must not be admitted or dispatched; Professor cannot override these limits or physical capacity.
requirements.statement: Reject over-quota admission and dispatch; require a free node with enough capacity.
assumptions: Requested runtime is an admission limit, not an elapsed-time watchdog. Dispatch combines WithinJobQuota and FreeCompatible in P5.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: **Information flow and isolation:** PhD and Master keep their work private from each other, while Professor may inspect both students' work.
requirements.statement: Gate single-job reads and retain original bulk/private filtering.
assumptions: Readable gates single-job reads. Original view/read_private still filter their own results. QueueViewer and PrivateReadable are currently analysis-only. Datalog can derive visible record/field IDs for a trusted result adapter to project before disclosure; that projection is not yet connected.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Neither student may receive the other's private job specifications, inputs, results, approvals or execution receipts through tools, model contexts or messages.
requirements.statement: Prevent peer disclosure across every output channel.
assumptions: Tool reads are scoped, but message/context IFC is incomplete. The original T2 UNSAFE_PEER_NOTE delivers private PhD data to Master outside the completion-report guard. Trusted adapters must bind actual data versions and record DependsOn before release; agents cannot supply trusted lineage. Professor mixed-private contexts also require a precision/usability decision.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Students may send their own task details to Professor, who may inspect both students' records and share private details only with the owning student.
requirements.statement: Permit owner-to-Professor sharing and owner-specific replies.
assumptions: No general send/receive IFC gate is installed. The P1.3 decorator checks only structured completion-report ownership; arbitrary body text and other message types remain unmediated.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Forbidden and nonexistent job lookups must both return UNAVAILABLE without revealing whether a private record exists.
requirements.statement: Return the same public response for a forbidden or missing job.
assumptions: No matching Readable means no Allow. The adapter returns the original UNAVAILABLE shape without executing the read.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Role quotas, node specifications and aggregate busy/free availability are public; this boundary does not prevent inference from public timing or availability.
requirements.statement: Keep quotas, node capacity and aggregate availability public.
assumptions: The original Store.view returns public capacity/availability and omits allocation tokens. No view-to-EDB mapping runs; timing inference remains outside scope.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: The authorized evaluator may inspect complete synthetic traces, but student agents must not receive that full view.
requirements.statement: Restrict full evaluator traces to the evaluator.
assumptions: The original Trace/export machinery is unchanged and not exposed by these tools. Deployment and any export endpoint must separately preserve this boundary.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: API credentials must never appear in agent prompts, traces or submitted files.
requirements.statement: Keep credentials out of prompts, traces and submissions.
assumptions: No credential detector or complete secret-flow instrumentation is installed. Do not translate this obligation into a fictitious always-successful rule.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: **Evidence for job decisions:** Starting a job requires a current approval record; marking it completed requires a matching runner receipt.
requirements.statement: Require recorded approval to start and recorded runner evidence to finish.
assumptions: P3.2 and P3.5 give the two exact joins. A natural-language agent claim creates neither record.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Before dispatch, require a successful Professor approval record matching the job's current task version and exact resource request.
requirements.statement: Match approval to the current job version, exact spec and policy.
assumptions: The original approve method returns its actual approval. The tool helper records Approval, ApprovalSpec and CurrentApproval without reading Store.snapshot.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Only QUEUED jobs may be revised; a revision invalidates the approval and requires another review.
requirements.statement: Revise only QUEUED work and invalidate the old approval.
assumptions: The unchanged Store.revise increments the version and clears approval. The adapter records the returned Job/JobSpec/CurrentApproval; re-evaluation removes the previous MatchingApproval answer.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Approval leaves the job QUEUED without reserving a node.
requirements.statement: Approval records evidence without allocating a node or starting a job.
assumptions: Original approval stores evidence without changing business state. Its confirmed result updates policy inputs, with no ResourceState transition.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Before marking a job COMPLETED, require a prior simulator-issued completion receipt for that job's current run.
requirements.statement: Complete only with a successful simulator receipt for the current run and allocation.
assumptions: The original simulator returns its receipt; the adapter records it and its dependencies. Original finish confirms the completed job and release before the runtime commits the policy-state transition.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: These records must identify their source and the task or run they support.
requirements.statement: Retain the origin and supported task/run of each decision record.
assumptions: Successful original tool results supply record IDs and references; the tool helper records Source and DependsOn in one EDB batch. This is decision-record lineage, not complete message/context IFC, and does not authenticate contents.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: **Four-state lifecycle and exclusive ownership:** Jobs follow the allowed state transitions, and a node belongs to at most one running job at a time.
requirements.statement: Use the declared lifecycle and preserve exclusive allocations.
assumptions: P4.2-P4.8 separate the state graph from actual backend state and allocation consistency.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: The only states are QUEUED, RUNNING, COMPLETED and TERMINATED.
requirements.statement: Admit only QUEUED, RUNNING, COMPLETED and TERMINATED.
assumptions: The Datalog invariant checks admitted state labels. ResourceState is a single current row per resource; the runtime removes the old value on confirmed transition.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Submission creates QUEUED.
requirements.statement: Create each new job in QUEUED.
assumptions: Original Store.submit creates the job and returns its ID/state. The adapter puts ResourceType and the returned ResourceState. Before committing, runtime checks new resources against InitialState("job", "QUEUED"); tool updates cannot reset existing resource state.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Allowed transitions are QUEUED to RUNNING or TERMINATED, and RUNNING to COMPLETED or TERMINATED.
requirements.statement: Declare type-level edges for dispatch, completion, rejection and stop.
assumptions: The static typed edges live in rules.dl. Allow rules check CanTransition; after the effect confirms success, the runtime replaces the old ResourceState atomically.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Rejected requests and queued cancellations end in TERMINATED.
requirements.statement: Terminate a rejected or cancelled queued request.
assumptions: The adapter maps approve_job(false) to reject_job. Datalog checks the transition; the runtime commits TERMINATED only after success.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Entry to RUNNING requires the approval in P3 and successful allocation of a free compatible node.
requirements.statement: Enter RUNNING only after valid approval and successful free-node allocation.
assumptions: Datalog checks dispatchability and lifecycle before calling original Store.dispatch. The returned run confirms allocation; its result adapter stages policy run/node changes with the selected state transition.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Each RUNNING job must own exactly one matching active allocation, and each node may belong to at most one running job.
requirements.statement: Require a consistent job/run/node allocation before and after every guarded operation.
assumptions: Datalog checks policy allocation consistency before and after effects. A failed postcondition discards staged EDB edits and stops the session, but does not undo an already committed Store operation. No shared Store/EDB transaction is claimed.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Terminal jobs must not restart; another attempt requires a new submission.
requirements.statement: Never dispatch a terminal job; retries require a new submission.
assumptions: Dispatchable requires QUEUED. Declared terminal self-loops acknowledge repeated stop requests without changing facts.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: P6 defines the release procedure that preserves this ownership invariant.
requirements.statement: Release allocations only through the P6 confirmation procedure.
assumptions: No extra rule is needed for this cross-reference.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: **Waiting-queue order:** PhD normally goes first, with protection against indefinite Master waiting.
requirements.statement: Prefer PhD while waiting and promote sufficiently skipped Master jobs.
assumptions: Priority is enforced at a guarded dispatch. The rules do not force Professor or any scheduler to make future dispatch calls.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: When eligible queued jobs compete for the same free compatible node, select PhD before Master.
requirements.statement: Compare only eligible queued candidates selecting the same free compatible node.
assumptions: Eligible and Outranked use current EDB facts. Original Store.dispatch retains its own scheduler and may refuse; the adapter records the actual returned run, not a reimplemented business scheduler.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Priority applies only while waiting and must not interrupt a running job.
requirements.statement: Apply priority only to QUEUED work without preempting RUNNING jobs.
assumptions: Priority and Eligible require QUEUED; FreeCompatible requires an empty node token. A Professor stop remains a separate P6 operation.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: A Master job that remains eligible but is skipped at three compatible dispatch opportunities must receive higher priority than PhD jobs.
requirements.statement: After three actual competing opportunities, promote Master above PhD.
assumptions: For this pinned one-node-per-type cluster, the returned run.candidate_order identifies the competitors whose counters Store increments. The adapter updates their keyed Waiting rows. More general allocation semantics need an explicit backend delta.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Equal priorities use submission order.
requirements.statement: Break equal-priority competition by submission order.
assumptions: The second Outranked clause uses the original submission sequence, not wall-clock timestamps.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: An unrelated GPU request must not prevent a compatible Master job from using a free CPU node.
requirements.statement: Do not let an unrelated GPU job block an eligible CPU job.
assumptions: Outranked joins on the selected node, so different node candidates do not compete.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: **Stop confirmation and safe node release:** Release a node only after confirmed completion or stopping, and only for the run that currently owns it.
requirements.statement: Release only a confirmed current allocation.
assumptions: The unchanged Store owns business completion, stop and release. The adapter records successful results in the policy EDB. The two stores have no shared transaction; uncertain post-effect errors stop the session.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: A stop or cancellation request must record a specific reason.
requirements.statement: Require a bounded nonblank reason and retain it with the stop.
assumptions: The original bounded_text helper validates text and StopReason retains it as a fact. Semantic specificity is not classified.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Keep a RUNNING job's state and allocation until the simulator confirms its current run has stopped; a failed stop releases nothing.
requirements.statement: Keep RUNNING state and allocation until the local runner confirms stop.
assumptions: A failed original stop returns ok=false, so the tool skips fact updates and the policy-state transition. Original trace snapshots are unchanged; no Store-to-EDB projection runs.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Following valid completion under P3 or a confirmed stop, release exactly that run's allocation after matching both run ID and allocation generation against the node's current owner.
requirements.statement: Match current run ID and allocation generation before release.
assumptions: The original Store matches run/generation before releasing the node. Its confirmed job result causes the adapter to record the policy node release; runtime then commits the selected policy-state transition.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: A mismatch, duplicate or delayed notification must leave any newer allocation unchanged; handling the same terminal notification again must have no new effect.
requirements.statement: Ignore stale/duplicate completion and make terminal stop acknowledgement harmless.
assumptions: A stale completion has no matching current permission. Terminal stop self-loops return an acknowledgement without a new release or fact change.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: For example, Master's old notification must not release a node reassigned to a newer PhD run.
requirements.statement: An old Master notification must not release a newer PhD allocation.
assumptions: This source sentence is an example of those checks, not another predicate or rule.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.

requirements.source: Role permissions are defined in P1.
requirements.statement: Use the P1 owner/Professor stop permissions.
assumptions: No additional grant or agent fact is introduced.
Only adapted tools are mediated; backend identity and records are authoritative.
